changelog.change: Initial shape: the eleven published columns, typed, with canonical_url, url_key and detail refused at import.
changelog.why: The only thing standing between the item-health census and a browser was a tuple of eleven strings in publish_telemetry.py and a set of three more it was checked against. Both are readable code and neither is a contract, so the projection had no schema, no version stamp and no changelog while every other persisted surface has all three (Rule #3). Typing it also gives the migration something to read a committed shard back through, which is what proves a published file still loads rather than merely still parses. item_id is the one cell carried as an opaque key: identity is minted by ItemHealthRow, and a published shard has no writer left to re-mint it if that grammar moves.

source_words_before_cap.description: Words in the extracted body before extract.truncation_cap_tokens cut it. A count of our own extraction, never the text, so it crosses on the same terms source_words always has. Empty on every row written before 2026-08-28, and empty means unknown rather than uncut.
